course.title: Meal Prep Business
course.tagline: Plan, cook and sell weekly meal prep boxes that busy people reorder.

days.title: What Is Meal Prep?
days.goal: Know what meal prep is and who buys it.

video.title: How to Start a Thriving Meal Prep Business from Scratch

steps: Meal prep means cooking meals in advance for the week.
Customers are busy people who want healthy food without cooking.
You cook once or twice a week and deliver boxes for the week.
Each box has a main, a side, and sometimes a snack.
Meal prep saves customers time. That is what they pay for.
days.task: Write down who your customers are and why they would buy from you.
days.challenge: List three people you know who might buy meal prep boxes.

quiz.q: What is meal prep?
options: Cooking meals in advance for the week
quiz.explain: Meal prep is cooking meals ahead for the week.

quiz.q: Who buys meal prep?
options: Busy people who want healthy food without cooking
quiz.explain: Busy people buy meal prep to save time.

quiz.q: What is in a meal prep box?
options: A main, a side, and sometimes a snack
quiz.explain: A box has a main, a side, and sometimes a snack.

days.title: Plan Your First Meal Prep Menu
days.goal: Plan a weekly menu with variety.

video.title: Selling Meal Prep - Feeding the Health Freaks

steps: Pick 3 or 4 mains for the week. Keep it simple.
Offer variety: chicken, fish, beef, and a vegetarian option.
Each meal needs a protein, a carb (like rice), and vegetables.
Use ingredients that stay tasty for days.
Write the menu with prices per box.
days.task: Plan a weekly menu with 4 mains.
days.challenge: Write the price per box for each meal.

quiz.q: What should each meal prep box have?
options: A protein, a carb, and vegetables
quiz.explain: A good box has protein, a carb like rice, and vegetables.

quiz.q: Why offer variety?
options: So customers do not get bored
quiz.explain: Variety keeps customers ordering every week.

quiz.q: Why use ingredients that stay tasty?
options: Food must taste good on day 4, not just day 1
quiz.explain: Meal prep food is eaten days later, so it must stay tasty.

days.title: Cooking Rice for Meal Prep
days.goal: Cook rice that stays good for days.

video.title: How to Price Your Food Product Series: Pricing Homemade Food

steps: Rinse rice until the water runs clear.
Use 1 part rice to 1.5 parts water.
Cook on low heat with the lid on. Do not lift the lid.
Rest for 10 minutes, then fluff with a fork.
Cool fast in shallow containers before packing.
days.task: Cook a big pot of rice for meal prep.
days.challenge: Pack it into boxes and check it after 2 days.

quiz.q: Why rinse rice?
options: To remove starch so it stays separate
quiz.explain: Rinsing removes starch so rice stays fluffy.

quiz.q: Why not lift the lid while rice cooks?
options: It lets steam out and ruins the cooking
quiz.explain: Rice cooks in trapped steam. Lifting the lid lets it out.

quiz.q: Why cool rice fast before packing?
quiz.explain: Rice must cool fast so germs cannot grow.

days.title: Roast Chicken for the Week
days.goal: Roast chicken and vegetables for meal prep boxes.

video.title: How to Start Selling Homemade Meals from Home?

steps: Season chicken with salt, pepper, and garlic.
Cut vegetables into similar sizes.
Roast at 200°C until the chicken reaches 75°C inside.
Rest for 10 minutes before cutting.
Cut into portions and pack with vegetables and rice.
days.task: Roast a chicken with vegetables and pack 4 boxes.
days.challenge: Taste a box on day 3 and note if it is still good.

quiz.q: What temperature must chicken reach?
quiz.explain: Chicken must reach 75°C inside to be safe.

quiz.q: Why rest chicken before cutting?
options: Juices spread back so the meat stays moist
quiz.explain: Resting keeps the juices in the meat.

quiz.q: Why cut vegetables into similar sizes?
options: So they cook at the same rate
quiz.explain: Even sizes cook evenly.

days.title: Chicken Fried Rice for Boxes
days.goal: Make chicken fried rice that packs well.

video.title: Beginners Guide to Meal Prep (Meal Prep Ideas!)

steps: Use cold, day-old rice. Fresh rice turns mushy.
Fry chicken first, then set it aside.
Fry onion, garlic, and vegetables.
Add rice and soy sauce. Toss on high heat.
Cool fast and pack into boxes.
days.task: Make chicken fried rice and pack 4 boxes.
days.challenge: Taste a box on day 2 and day 4. Compare.

quiz.q: Why use day-old rice for fried rice?
options: Cold rice stays separate instead of turning mushy
quiz.explain: Cold, dry rice fries into separate grains.

quiz.q: Why fry chicken first and set it aside?
options: So it does not overcook while the rice fries
quiz.explain: Chicken cooked first and added back at the end stays tender.

quiz.q: Why cool fried rice fast?
quiz.explain: Rice must cool fast to stay safe.

days.title: Packing Boxes: Keep Food Fresh
days.goal: Pack meal prep boxes so food stays fresh.

video.title: How to Cook Rice

steps: Use food-grade containers that seal tightly.
Cool food fully before packing. Warm food makes steam and goes soggy.
Pack rice, protein, and vegetables in separate parts of the box.
Label with the meal name and the date.
Store boxes in the fridge. Use within 4 days.
days.task: Pack 4 meal prep boxes.
days.challenge: Label them and store them in the fridge.

quiz.q: Why cool food before packing?
options: Warm food makes steam and goes soggy
quiz.explain: Warm food in a closed box makes steam, which makes food soggy.

quiz.q: How long do meal prep boxes keep in the fridge?
quiz.explain: Cooked meal prep boxes keep up to 4 days in the fridge.

quiz.q: Why label boxes?
options: So customers know what it is and when it was made
quiz.explain: Labels tell the customer what the meal is and when it was made.

days.title: Week 1 Project: A Week of Boxes
days.goal: Cook and pack a full week of meal prep boxes.

video.title: How to Cook Roast Chicken and Vegetables

steps: Plan the menu: 4 mains for the week.
Write the shopping list and costs.
Cook everything in one day: rice, chicken, fried rice, and vegetables.
Pack 8 to 12 boxes and label them.
Eat one box each day and note how it tastes on day 4.
days.task: Cook and pack a week of boxes for yourself.
days.challenge: Cost the week and work out the price per box.

quiz.q: Why cook everything in one day?
options: One big cook saves time and gas for the week
quiz.explain: Cooking once for the week saves time and gas.

quiz.q: Why label every box?
options: So you know what it is and when it was made
quiz.explain: Labels stop mix-ups and show freshness.

quiz.q: Why cost the week?
options: So you know the price per box
quiz.explain: Costing tells you what to charge per box.

project.title: Cook a Week of Meal Prep Boxes
project.brief: Cook and pack 8 to 12 boxes for the week.
checks: Rice, chicken, and fried rice cooked

days.title: Pricing Meal Prep Boxes
days.goal: Set prices that make a profit.

video.title: Chicken Fried Rice

steps: List every ingredient with its price.
Add the cost of the box, packaging, and delivery.
Add your time: how many hours did you cook?
Divide the total by the number of boxes.
Charge 2 to 3 times the food cost for a profit.
days.task: Cost one week of boxes and set the price per box.
days.challenge: Compare your price with meal prep sellers near you.

quiz.q: What is the cost per box?
options: Total cost divided by the number of boxes
quiz.explain: Cost per box is the total cost shared across all the boxes you made.

quiz.q: Why charge 2 to 3 times the food cost?
options: To cover packaging, delivery, and your time, and still make a profit
quiz.explain: The extra covers all costs beyond food and leaves profit.

quiz.q: What else must you add to the cost?
quiz.explain: Boxes, packaging, and delivery are real costs.

days.title: Healthy Meal Prep: Balanced Boxes
days.goal: Make healthy, balanced meal prep boxes.

video.title: Chicken Egg Fried Rice

steps: Each box needs protein, a carb, and vegetables.
Use less oil and salt. Use herbs and spices for flavour.
Offer a low-carb option: more vegetables, less rice.
Offer a high-protein option for gym customers.
Write the calories on the label if you can.
days.task: Make a healthy box with less oil and salt.
days.challenge: Make a high-protein box for gym customers.

quiz.q: What makes a box balanced?
quiz.explain: A balanced box has protein, a carb, and vegetables.

quiz.q: How do you cut salt without losing flavour?
quiz.explain: Herbs, spices, and peppers add flavour so you need less salt.

quiz.q: What is a high-protein box?
options: A box with extra meat, eggs, or beans
quiz.explain: A high-protein box has extra meat, eggs, or beans.

days.title: Pasta for Meal Prep
days.goal: Cook pasta that stays good in boxes.

video.title: How to Cook Pasta

steps: Cook pasta until it is just firm, not soft.
Toss with a little oil so it does not stick.
Cool fast in shallow containers.
Pack with sauce separately so pasta does not go soggy.
Reheat with a splash of water.
days.task: Cook pasta and pack 4 boxes.
days.challenge: Taste a box on day 3 and note if it is still good.

quiz.q: Why cook pasta just firm for meal prep?
options: It softens a little when reheated
quiz.explain: Pasta cooked firm stays good after reheating. Soft pasta turns mushy.

quiz.q: Why pack sauce separately?
options: So pasta does not go soggy
quiz.explain: Sauce mixed in early soaks into pasta and makes it soggy.

quiz.q: Why add water when reheating pasta?
quiz.explain: A splash of water keeps pasta moist when reheated.

days.title: Smoothies for Meal Prep
days.goal: Add a smoothie to your meal prep boxes.

video.title: How to Make a Smoothie

steps: Make a smoothie with banana, mango, and milk.
Pour into small bottles with tight lids.
Label with the date. Drink within 2 days.
Offer a smoothie as an extra with a box.
Charge a little extra for the smoothie.
days.task: Make smoothies and add them to your boxes.
days.challenge: Price a box with a smoothie and a box without.

quiz.q: How long does a smoothie keep?
quiz.explain: Fresh smoothies are best within 2 days.

quiz.q: Why offer a smoothie with a box?
options: It adds value and customers like it
quiz.explain: A smoothie makes the box feel like a full meal.

quiz.q: Why charge extra for a smoothie?
options: It costs fruit and a bottle
quiz.explain: A smoothie has its own costs, so it has its own price.

days.title: Finding Customers: Who Needs Meal Prep?
days.goal: Find your first meal prep customers.

video.title: How to Start a Thriving Meal Prep Business from Scratch

steps: Busy workers, gym goers, and students are good customers.
Tell friends and family first. Ask them to share.
Post your menu and prices on WhatsApp and social media.
Offer a free sample box to your first customers.
Ask happy customers to tell their friends.
days.task: Post your meal prep menu on WhatsApp or social media.
days.challenge: Offer a free sample box to one person.

quiz.q: Who buys meal prep?
options: Busy workers, gym goers, and students
quiz.explain: Busy workers, gym goers, and students are the main buyers.

quiz.q: Why offer a free sample box?
options: So people taste your food and order more
quiz.explain: A free sample lets people taste your food before they pay.

quiz.q: Why ask customers to tell friends?
options: Word of mouth is the best free advert
quiz.explain: Happy customers telling friends is the cheapest marketing.

days.title: Weekly Subscriptions: Regular Income
days.goal: Sell weekly subscriptions for steady income.

video.title: Selling Meal Prep - Feeding the Health Freaks

steps: A subscription means a customer pays for a week of boxes in advance.
Offer 5 boxes a week (Monday to Friday) or 7 boxes.
Give a small discount for a weekly subscription.
Take payment in advance. Do not cook without payment.
Deliver on the same days each week so customers can plan.
days.task: Plan a weekly subscription: 5 boxes, price, and delivery days.
days.challenge: Offer it to three people and ask what they think.

quiz.q: What is a weekly subscription?
options: Paying in advance for a week of boxes
quiz.explain: A subscription is payment in advance for a week of boxes.

quiz.q: Why take payment in advance?
options: So you do not cook food nobody pays for
quiz.explain: Advance payment means you cook only what is sold.

quiz.q: Why deliver on the same days each week?
quiz.explain: Regular delivery days help customers plan their week.

days.title: Week 2 Project: Sell Your First Boxes
days.goal: Sell your first meal prep boxes to real customers.

video.title: How to Price Your Food Product Series: Pricing Homemade Food

steps: Plan the menu and take orders in advance.
Cook everything in one day.
Pack boxes neatly and label them.
Deliver on time to your customers.
Ask for feedback and work out your profit.
days.task: Sell meal prep boxes to at least 3 customers.
days.challenge: Work out your sales, costs, and profit.

quiz.q: Why take orders in advance?
options: So you cook only what is sold
quiz.explain: Advance orders mean no waste and no guessing.

quiz.q: Why deliver on time?
quiz.explain: On-time delivery builds trust.

quiz.q: Why ask for feedback?
options: It tells you what to improve
quiz.explain: Feedback shows what customers liked and what to fix.

project.title: Sell Your First Meal Prep Boxes
project.brief: Cook, pack, and deliver boxes to at least 3 customers.
checks: Menu planned and orders taken in advance
Sales, costs, and profit worked out

days.title: Food Safety for Meal Prep
days.goal: Keep meal prep food safe.

video.title: How to Start Selling Homemade Meals from Home?

steps: Cool food fast, within 2 hours.
Store boxes in the fridge below 5°C.
Use boxes within 4 days. Freeze extras.
Label every box with the date.
Tell customers to reheat until steaming hot.
days.task: Do a food safety check of your meal prep work.
days.challenge: Write a food safety list for your business.

quiz.q: How fast must food cool?
quiz.explain: Food must cool within 2 hours to stay safe.

quiz.q: How long do boxes keep in the fridge?
quiz.explain: Meal prep boxes keep up to 4 days in the fridge.

quiz.q: Why tell customers to reheat until steaming hot?
options: So the food is safe to eat
quiz.explain: Reheating until steaming hot kills germs.

days.title: Freezing Meal Prep Boxes
days.goal: Freeze boxes so they last longer.

video.title: Beginners Guide to Meal Prep (Meal Prep Ideas!)

steps: Freeze boxes you will not eat within 4 days.
Use freezer-safe containers.
Label with the meal name and date.
Thaw in the fridge overnight, never on the counter.
Eat within 1 month of freezing.
days.task: Freeze 4 boxes and label them.
days.challenge: Thaw one box in the fridge and reheat it properly.

quiz.q: When should you freeze a box?
options: If you will not eat it within 4 days
quiz.explain: Freeze boxes you will not eat within 4 days.

quiz.q: How do you thaw a frozen box?
quiz.explain: Thawing in the fridge keeps food cold and safe.

quiz.q: How long do frozen boxes keep?
quiz.explain: Frozen meal prep boxes are best within 1 month.

days.title: Delivery: Get Boxes to Customers
days.goal: Deliver meal prep boxes safely and on time.

video.title: How to Cook Rice

steps: Use a cooler bag with ice to keep boxes cold.
Plan your delivery route: nearest first, furthest last.
Tell customers the delivery time in advance.
Deliver on time, every time.
Ask customers to put boxes in the fridge at once.
days.task: Plan a delivery route for 5 customers.
days.challenge: Deliver boxes using a cooler bag.

quiz.q: Why use a cooler bag?
options: It keeps boxes cold during delivery
quiz.explain: A cooler bag keeps food at a safe temperature.

quiz.q: Why plan your route?
options: So deliveries are fast and on time
quiz.explain: A planned route saves time and keeps food cold.

quiz.q: Why tell customers the delivery time?
options: So they are home to receive the boxes
quiz.explain: Customers must be home to put boxes in the fridge at once.

days.title: Seasonal Menus: Change with the Seasons
days.goal: Change your menu with the seasons.

video.title: How to Cook Roast Chicken and Vegetables

steps: Use fruit and vegetables in season. They are cheaper and tastier.
Offer light meals in hot weather and hearty meals in cold weather.
Change your menu every month or two.
Ask customers what they want next.
Keep your best sellers. Drop what does not sell.
days.task: Plan a new seasonal menu.
days.challenge: Ask three customers what they would like next.

quiz.q: Why use food in season?
options: It is cheaper and tastes better
quiz.explain: Food in season is fresh, cheap, and full of flavour.

quiz.q: Why change your menu?
options: So customers do not get bored
quiz.explain: A changing menu keeps customers ordering.

quiz.q: Why drop dishes that do not sell?
options: So you do not waste food and time
quiz.explain: A dish that does not sell wastes food and money.

days.title: Meal Prep Business: First Steps
days.goal: Take your first steps toward a meal prep business.

video.title: Chicken Fried Rice

steps: Pick 3 or 4 mains to offer. Keep the menu small.
Set your prices from your costing work.
Take clear photos of your boxes in good light.
Tell friends and family first. Ask them to share.
Take orders in advance so you cook only what is sold.
days.task: Take photos of your best boxes and show them to three people.
days.challenge: Take one real order, even a small one, and deliver it on time.

quiz.q: Why start with only 3 or 4 mains?
options: A small menu is easier to cook well and cost
quiz.explain: A small menu keeps quality high and costing simple.

quiz.q: Why take orders in advance?
options: So you cook only what is sold and waste nothing
quiz.explain: Advance orders mean no waste and no guessing.

quiz.q: Why do photos matter?
options: Clear photos help people decide to buy
quiz.explain: People buy with their eyes first. Good photos sell boxes.

days.title: Meal Prep Mistakes and Fixes
days.goal: Fix the commonest meal prep problems.

video.title: Chicken Egg Fried Rice

steps: Food went soggy? Pack sauce separately and cool food fully first.
Food went bad fast? Check your fridge temperature and cooling time.
Customers got bored? Change your menu and add new dishes.
Orders are late? Cook earlier and plan your route better.
Write down each problem and fix.
days.task: Fix one meal prep problem you have had.
days.challenge: Write a list of three things you will do better next week.

quiz.q: What do you do if food went soggy?
options: Pack sauce separately and cool food fully first
quiz.explain: Separate sauce and full cooling stop soggy food.

quiz.q: What do you do if food went bad fast?
options: Check fridge temperature and cooling time
quiz.explain: A warm fridge or slow cooling makes food go bad fast.

quiz.q: What do you do if customers got bored?
options: Change the menu and add new dishes
quiz.explain: A new menu keeps customers interested.

days.title: Week 3 Project: A Subscription Week
days.goal: Run a full subscription week for real customers.

video.title: How to Cook Pasta

steps: Take weekly orders in advance with payment.
Plan the menu: 5 different boxes for the week.
Cook everything in one or two days.
Pack, label, and deliver on schedule.
Ask for feedback and work out your profit.
days.task: Run a subscription week for at least 3 customers.
days.challenge: Work out your sales, costs, and profit.

quiz.q: Why take payment in advance?
options: So you do not cook food nobody pays for
quiz.explain: Advance payment means you cook only what is sold.

quiz.q: Why plan 5 different boxes?
options: Variety keeps customers happy all week
quiz.explain: Five different boxes stop customers getting bored.

quiz.q: Why ask for feedback after the week?
options: It tells you what to improve next week
quiz.explain: Feedback after a full week shows what worked.

project.title: Run a Subscription Week
project.brief: Deliver 5 boxes to at least 3 customers for a full week.
checks: Weekly orders taken with payment in advance
Sales, costs, and profit worked out

days.title: Growing: From Home Kitchen to Bigger
days.goal: Grow your meal prep business step by step.

video.title: How to Make a Smoothie

steps: Start at home. Do small orders well.
Save profit to buy better containers and equipment.
Add one new dish each month.
Hire a helper when orders get too big for one person.
Do not take big orders until you are ready for them.
days.task: Write a growth plan for your meal prep business.
days.challenge: List one piece of equipment you want to buy next.

quiz.q: How do you grow a meal prep business?
options: Do small orders well and grow step by step
quiz.explain: Doing small orders well builds a good name. Growth follows.

quiz.q: Why save profit for equipment?
options: Better equipment lets you take bigger orders
quiz.explain: Good equipment makes bigger orders possible.

quiz.q: Why not take big orders too soon?
options: A failed big order can ruin your name
quiz.explain: A big order done badly hurts your name. Grow into it.

days.title: Marketing Your Meal Prep Business
days.goal: Tell people about your meal prep business.

video.title: How to Start a Thriving Meal Prep Business from Scratch

steps: Take clear photos of every box you make.
Post your menu and prices on WhatsApp and social media.
Ask happy customers to share your photos and number.
Offer a discount for a first weekly subscription.
Keep a list of past customers and message them about new menus.
days.task: Post your meal prep menu on WhatsApp or social media.
days.challenge: Ask a happy customer to share your number with a friend.

quiz.q: Why post photos of boxes?
options: Good photos help people decide to buy
quiz.explain: People buy with their eyes first. Good photos sell boxes.

quiz.q: Why offer a discount for a first subscription?
quiz.explain: A first-time discount gives people a reason to try you.

quiz.q: Why keep a list of past customers?
options: So you can tell them about new menus
quiz.explain: Past customers are the easiest people to sell to again.

days.title: Keeping Records: Orders and Money
days.goal: Keep simple records of your meal prep business.

video.title: Selling Meal Prep - Feeding the Health Freaks

steps: Write down every order: what, how many, who, and when.
Write down what you spent and what you earned.
Work out your profit each week.
Note which boxes sell best and which do not.
Keep your money for meal prep separate from your spending money.
days.task: Start a simple order book today, on paper or on your phone.
days.challenge: Work out your profit from one week of boxes.

quiz.q: Why write down every order?
options: So nothing is forgotten and you know what to cook
quiz.explain: Written orders stop mistakes and show what sells.

quiz.q: What is profit?
options: What is left after costs are taken from what you earned
quiz.explain: Profit is what remains after you pay for food, boxes, and delivery.

quiz.q: Why keep meal prep money separate?
options: So you always know if the business is making money
quiz.explain: Separate money shows the true profit of your business.

days.title: Your Signature Meal Prep Box
days.goal: Choose and perfect one box you can make brilliantly.

video.title: How to Price Your Food Product Series: Pricing Homemade Food

steps: Pick the box your customers love most from this course.
Write it down with exact amounts, costs, and prices.
Cook it again, timing every step and noting problems.
Fix the problems and cook it once more.
Get feedback from someone who ate it.
days.task: Cook your signature box and write the final version down.
days.challenge: Serve it to someone new and record what they say.

quiz.q: What is a signature box?
options: A box you can make brilliantly every time
A box with a fancy name
quiz.explain: A signature box is one you have mastered.

quiz.q: Why write exact amounts?
options: So you can repeat it the same way every time
quiz.explain: Exact amounts mean the same great box every time.

quiz.q: Why get a new person to taste it?
quiz.explain: People who know you may be polite. New tasters are honest.

days.title: Meal Prep for Special Diets
days.goal: Make boxes for special diets.

video.title: How to Start Selling Homemade Meals from Home?

steps: Low-carb: more vegetables and protein, less rice.
Vegetarian: beans, eggs, and vegetables instead of meat.
High-protein: extra meat, eggs, or beans for gym customers.
Ask customers about allergies before you cook.
Label every box with what is in it.
days.task: Make a vegetarian box.
days.challenge: Make a low-carb box and compare.

quiz.q: What is a low-carb box?
options: More vegetables and protein, less rice
quiz.explain: A low-carb box has more vegetables and protein and less rice.

quiz.q: What is a vegetarian box?
options: Beans, eggs, and vegetables instead of meat
quiz.explain: A vegetarian box uses beans, eggs, and vegetables for protein.

quiz.q: Why label every box?
options: So customers know what is in it
quiz.explain: Labels help customers with diets and allergies choose safely.

days.title: Customer Service for Meal Prep
days.goal: Serve meal prep customers well.

video.title: Beginners Guide to Meal Prep (Meal Prep Ideas!)

steps: Reply to messages fast. Customers like quick answers.
Deliver on time, every time.
If a box is wrong, fix it fast and say sorry.
Ask for feedback every week.
Thank customers and invite them to order again.
days.task: Practise replying to a customer message fast and politely.
days.challenge: Write a short message to thank a customer.

quiz.q: Why reply fast to messages?
quiz.explain: Fast replies show you care and win orders.

quiz.q: What do you do if a box is wrong?
options: Fix it fast and say sorry
quiz.explain: A fast fix and an apology can save the customer.

quiz.q: Why ask for feedback every week?
quiz.explain: Weekly feedback keeps your food and service good.

days.title: Meal Prep Trends: What Customers Want
days.goal: Learn what meal prep customers want now.

video.title: How to Cook Rice

steps: Customers want healthy, tasty food that is ready to eat.
Customers want clear labels with ingredients and calories.
Customers want easy ordering on WhatsApp.
Customers want food that stays fresh for days.
Ask your customers what they want and offer it.
days.task: Ask three people what they want from meal prep.
days.challenge: List three trends you will use in your business.

quiz.q: What do meal prep customers want?
options: Healthy, tasty food that is ready to eat
quiz.explain: Customers want healthy, tasty, ready-to-eat food.

quiz.q: Why use clear labels?
options: So customers know what is in the box
quiz.explain: Clear labels help customers choose and trust you.

quiz.q: Why ask customers what they want?
options: So you can offer what they will buy
quiz.explain: Asking customers tells you what will sell.

days.title: Revision: The Meal Prep Skills Check
days.goal: Revisit the core skills of the course.

video.title: How to Cook Roast Chicken and Vegetables

steps: Cook rice for meal prep from memory.
Pack a box correctly from memory.
Cost a box from memory.
Name the food safety rules for meal prep.
List your three strongest skills and one to improve.
days.task: Cook and pack a week of boxes from memory, no notes.
days.challenge: Teach one meal prep skill to a friend or family member.

quiz.q: How long do boxes keep in the fridge?
quiz.explain: Meal prep boxes keep up to 4 days in the fridge.

quiz.q: Why cook from memory?
options: It proves you really know the steps
quiz.explain: Cooking without notes shows the skills are truly learned.

quiz.q: Why teach a skill to someone else?
options: Teaching proves you really know it
quiz.explain: If you can teach it, you truly understand it.

days.title: Capstone Prep: Plan Your Final Subscription Week
days.goal: Plan your capstone subscription week.

video.title: Chicken Fried Rice

steps: Choose your capstone menu: 5 boxes for the week.
Write the full shopping list with costs.
Write the cooking and delivery schedule.
Check you have every tool, box, and ingredient.
Do a trial run of the hardest dish if you have time.
days.task: Write your complete capstone plan and cost it.
days.challenge: Do a trial run of your hardest capstone dish today.

quiz.q: What should your capstone show?
options: Everything you learned: cooking, packing, costing, and selling
quiz.explain: The capstone proves the whole course.

quiz.q: Why write a delivery schedule?
options: So every customer gets food on time
quiz.explain: A delivery schedule keeps every customer happy.

quiz.q: Why do a trial run?
options: To find problems before the real week
quiz.explain: A trial run finds problems while there is still time to fix them.

capstone.title: The Meal Prep Business: A Full Subscription Week
capstone.brief: Run a full subscription week for real customers: take orders and payment in advance, cook 5 different boxes, pack and label them, deliver on schedule, and collect feedback. Work out your sales, costs, and profit.
checks: Weekly orders taken with payment in advance
Boxes cooked, packed, and labelled correctly
Food cooled fast and stored below 5°C
Sales, costs, and profit worked out
deliverables: A photo of your meal prep boxes
Your weekly menu with recipes, costs, and prices
Your signature box recipe written in your own words
A short note on what you learned and what you will improve next
